title: ServerFrame
description: Every frame the daemon sends. Adding a variant is a new major.

The error for one request, or for a frame without a readable
request.
One event for one subscription.

leftovers.description: What the abandon did not undo; also in `operation.result.partial`.

A test fixture, never installable.

eventKinds.description: Every event kind the daemon knows (`EventKind::KINDS`).

platform.description: Each platform capability and whether this Mac supports it.

CapabilityStatus.description: Whether a provider has one capability.

supported.description: Whether the provider revision declares it.

arch.description: The architecture it is built for.

blockedReason.description: Why the artifact is blocked; only for `blocked` artifacts.

dependencies.description: Its dependencies; null while `versions.json` does not record them.

downloadSize.description: The archive size in bytes; only for `available` artifacts.

installedSize.description: The unpacked size in bytes, once `versions.json` records it.

minOs.description:
The oldest OS version it runs on, such as `13.0`; only for
`available` artifacts.

os.description: The OS it is built for.

sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the archive, 64 lowercase hex characters; only for
`available` artifacts. Clients match installed runtimes and running
installs by it.

source.description:
The host of the first download URL and its first path segment,
such as `github.com/nats-io`.

CatalogEntryState.description: What this Mac can do with a catalog entry. Open.

oneOf.description: At least one version installs on this Mac.
The artifact for this Mac is blocked.

On the roadmap, without a package.

CatalogInfo.description: The facts about the catalog the daemon loaded.

contentSha256.description:
The content digest from `catalog.json`, 64 lowercase hex
characters.

host.description: The target of this Mac, which every install verdict is for.

loadedAt.description: When the daemon loaded it, for diagnostics.

outdated.description:
Whether the catalog was published more than 180 days before the
request.

publishedAt.description: When the catalog was published, from `catalog.json`.

trust.description: How far the catalog is trusted.

CatalogIssue.description: One thing wrong with an invalid entry.

location.description: Where in the file, such as `metadata.id`.

message.description: What is wrong, in lowercase English.

reason.description:
Which limit or rule, only for codes with a reason list, such as
`total_bytes` for `catalog_limit`.

CatalogSourceKind.description: Where a catalog came from. Open.

oneOf.description: The catalog inside the app bundle.
A catalog folder from `STACKLY_CATALOG_DIR`.
A source this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

CatalogVersion.description: One exact version of a provider.

install.description: Whether this version installs on this Mac.

support.description: One cell per OS, always `macos`, `linux`, then `windows`.

ClientKind.description:
The kinds of client. Open: a newer client may send a value an older
daemon reads as `unrecognized`.

oneOf.description: The `stackly` CLI.
The SwiftUI app.
A kind this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

done.description: What is done, such as bytes downloaded.

CreatedItemInfo.description:
One thing an operation created or claimed, which a cancel or an abandon
may undo. A custom item's payload is never sent.

kind.description: The item kind, such as `instance_tree` or `secret_ref`.

reference.description:
The item's reference: an ID, a secret reference, or
`<compensator>:<key>`.

CreatedState.description: Where one created item stands. Open.

oneOf.description: The operation recorded that it is about to create the item.
The item exists and belongs to the operation.
The item was undone.
The item stays, as part of the operation's result.
Undoing the item failed.
The item turned out to belong to someone else and was left alone.

connectionsRejected.description: Rejected peers, connections over the limit, and failed handshakes.

eventsDropped.description: Events lagging subscribers lost; may exceed `eventsPublished`.

framesRejected.description: Frames answered with a framing or payload error.

logLinesDropped.description: Log lines dropped because the queue was full or a write failed.

socketRebinds.description: Times the socket was bound again after it went missing.

recovery.description:
The recovery report while the registry is in recovery mode, else
null (spec 0005, spec 0006 AC-18).

subsystems.description: Each subsystem, by its fixed name (see [`subsystem`]).

DaemonHealthStatus.description:
The overall daemon status. Open: newer daemons may add values. Named
apart from the health of an instance (spec 0004 and 0012).

oneOf.description: The daemon is bound and running its start steps.
Every built subsystem is `ok`.
A built subsystem is `degraded` or `unavailable`.
The daemon is shutting down.
A status this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

DaemonIdentity.description: The daemon's version and process ID.

DaemonInfo.description: Reply of `daemon.get_info`: who the daemon is and where it keeps things.

protocol.description: The protocol version the daemon speaks.

registrySchema.description:
The registry's schema version once the registry opened ready, or
null while it opens, in recovery mode, or from an older daemon
(spec 0005).

secretStore.description:
The secret store and the keychain chosen at start, or null from an
older daemon (spec 0011).

serverInstanceId.description: The UUID v7 of this daemon run.

socketPath.description: The resolved path of the daemon socket.

uid.description: The daemon's Unix user ID, or null on a platform without one.

DaemonReconciling.description:
Content of `daemon.reconciling`, a daemon event published at the start
and at the end of the reconciliation.

DaemonRoots.description: The daemon's resolved (not canonical) roots, as lossy UTF-8 text.

rootOverride.description: Whether `STACKLY_ROOT` was set when the daemon started.

runtime.description: The runtime root, which holds the socket.

DependencyKind.description: Where an artifact dependency comes from. Open.

oneOf.description: Inside the artifact.
Another artifact Stackly installs.
Part of macOS.

EndpointPortMode.description: How an IP endpoint asked for its port. Open.

oneOf.description: Exactly the requested port.
Any free port, given when the process starts.
A mode this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

bound.description: True only after readiness succeeded for the current process.

host.description: The host of an IP endpoint.

name.description: The endpoint name from the manifest.

port.description:
The effective port: the bound one if there is one, else the `Fixed`
port; null for an `Auto` endpoint without a bound port.

portMode.description: How the port was asked for.

socketPath.description:
The socket path of a `unix` endpoint, null while its port is not
known.

EndpointTransport.description: The transport of an endpoint. Open.

oneOf.description: TCP.
UDP.
A Unix domain socket.
A transport this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

ErrorBody.description:
The error envelope every daemon error and every client side IPC error
uses (VAL-020).

`code`, `category`, `message`, `retryable`, and `details` are frozen
across majors, so peers of any major can always exchange
`protocol.major_mismatch`.

category.description: The category the catalog gives the code.

details.description: Extra facts, with keys only from the code's catalog entry.

fields.description: The params fields that failed, for `request.invalid_params`.

hint.description: A safe recovery step, in English.

items.description:
A structured list that does not fit in `details`, with the item
`kind` and field keys from the code's catalog entry.

message.description:
One safe English sentence: lowercase start, no trailing period, at
most 200 characters, never a secret.

retryable.description:
True only when the daemon guarantees the request had no effect, so
the exact same request may be sent again.

rule.description: The PRD rule ID behind the error, such as `BR-008`.

ErrorCategory.description:
What a client should do about an error. Closed: a new category is a new
protocol major. Feature 8 derives CLI exit codes from it.

oneOf.description: Fix the input; sending the same request again fails again.
The resource does not exist; refresh the snapshot.
State changed or the resource is in use; refresh, then decide.
Identity, peer, or trust was refused; never retry on its own.
The version, method, or capability is not supported.
The daemon or a dependency is not available yet; check `retryable`.
The work ran and failed.
A time limit passed; the outcome may be unknown, check the operation.
The work was cancelled.
A bug or a broken invariant in Stackly.

ErrorDetail.description: One extra fact on an error, as a key and a string value.

key.description: A camelCase key from the code's catalog entry.

requestId.description:
The request that failed, or null only when its `requestId` could not
be read.

ErrorItem.description:
One entry of a structured list on an error, such as one reference that
needs a secret (spec 0011) or one manifest issue (spec 0009).

`kind` and the field keys are plain strings, so a client always decodes
an error frame, even with an item kind it does not know yet.

fields.description: The item's facts, with keys from the code's catalog entry.

kind.description: The item kind from the code's catalog entry, such as `issue`.

resource.description: The resource the event is about.

revision.description: The resource's revision after the change.

sequence.description: Position in this daemon run, rising by one per published event.

subscriptionId.description: The subscription this event is delivered for.

EventCursor.description: A position in the event stream of one daemon run.

sequence.description: The last sequence seen; 0 means no event yet.

serverInstanceId.description: The daemon run the sequence belongs to.

EventKind.description:
What happened. Each kind is `<area>.<name>`; the owner of an area adds
its kinds here. Clients skip kinds they do not know through
[`EventProbe`], so a new kind is a minor bump.

oneOf.description: The subscriber missed events; take a new snapshot.
The daemon is shutting down.

An operation was created or changed state (spec 0007). The event's
resource is the operation and its revision the operation's.

An operation changed without changing state: stage, progress,
`waitingOn`, the point of no return, or a cancel (spec 0007).

A secret reference was stored, observed with another status,
restored, or deleted (spec 0011). The event's resource is
`{kind: secret, id: <reference>}`.

An instance changed in a way that raised its revision: created,
lifecycle, desired state, or an `Auto` port (spec 0010). The event's
resource is the instance and its revision the instance's.

The status of an instance changed (spec 0010). Clients apply it by
`statusSeq`, never by revision. The event's resource is the
instance.

An instance row was deleted (spec 0010). The event's revision is
the last revision plus one. Never sent before feature 20.

The supervisor started or finished reconciling instances with the
processes found after a daemon start (spec 0010). A daemon event:
no resource, no revision.

FieldError.description:
One params field that failed to decode or validate. An error carries at
most 32 of them (`FIELD_ERRORS_MAX`) and counts the rest in its
`omitted` detail.

code.description: A code from the fixed set in [`FieldCode`].

message.description: The fixed text of the code; never the input value.

path.description:
Where the field sits, relative to the params, such as `name`,
`since.sequence`, or `kinds[3]`. At most 256 characters.

GapReason.description: Why a subscriber missed events. Open: newer daemons may add values.

oneOf.description: The subscriber fell more than the event buffer behind.
The cursor is older than the replay ring.
The cursor belongs to another daemon run.
A reason this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

HandshakeAccepted.description:
Reply of `daemon.handshake` when the majors match and the params are
valid.

contractDrift.description:
True when the versions match but the digests differ: the connection
works, and the daemon logs one warning.

head.description:
The newest event cursor at handshake time; sequence 0 means no event
yet.

protocol.description: The protocol version the daemon speaks.

serverInstanceId.description: A fresh UUID v7 for each daemon run; event cursors belong to it.

IdentityBlocker.description: The content of the `dataInUse` and `identityUnproven` blockers.

IdentityCheckEntry.description: The result of one identity check, by name.

IdentityCheckName.description: The seven checks that prove a process belongs to an instance. Open.

oneOf.description: The boot ID now equals the recorded one.
A live process has the recorded PID.
Its start time equals the recorded one.
Its executable is the recorded canonical path.
It runs as the user running now.
Its session ID equals the recorded one.
It holds the instance lock file open.
A check this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

IdentityCheckResult.description:
The result of one identity check. Open. `not_checked` is spelled
`notChecked` on the wire.

oneOf.description: The check ran and passed.
The check ran and failed.

The check did not run, because an earlier one already decided the
outcome or an input was missing.
A result this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

IdentityEvidence.description:
What gathering evidence found about a process, in the order the checks
run. Checks that did not run are `notChecked`.

error.description: Redacted text of the error that stopped the gathering.

lock.description: The state of the instance lock.

pid.description: The PID of the recorded observation.

stopped.description:
True when the process is still suspended: its daemon died after
spawning it and before resuming it.

InstallVerdict.description: The install gate's verdict for one version on this Mac.

installable.description: Whether the version can be installed.

reason.description: Why not; null when it can.

InstanceActionAccepted.description:
The reply of `instance.start` and `instance.stop`.

An action that changes something starts an operation and returns it in
`accepted`. An instance already in the asked state answers
`alreadyInState` with no operation and no bound idempotency key.

accepted.description:
The operation, as created or as it stands now; null when nothing
ran.

alreadyInState.description: True when the instance was already in the asked state.

InstanceBlocker.description:
Why an instance cannot start or be trusted, one value with the priority
`identityUnproven`, then `dataInUse`, then `needsSecret`. A blocker this
build does not know makes the snapshot fail to decode, so a new blocker
is a protocol major.

oneOf.description:
A process matches the recorded identity but does not hold the
instance lock, or gathering the evidence failed.

A process Stackly cannot prove is the instance's own holds the
instance lock.
A secret the instance needs cannot be read (spec 0011).

InstanceDesired.description: Whether the person wants an instance running. Closed.

oneOf.description: The person wants it running.
The person wants it stopped.

InstanceHealth.description: Health as read now (`effective` at the time of the snapshot).

detail.description: Redacted text with more about the reason.

reason.description: A snake case code saying why.

InstanceHealthChanged.description:
Content of `instance.health_changed`: the status fields of an instance
after the effective readiness, health, blocker, restart status,
process, or log availability changed. A client applies it when
`statusSeq` is greater than the one it holds for the instance, whatever
the event's revision says.

blocker.description: Why the instance is blocked, if it is.

logsUnavailable.description: True when the output of the running process cannot be read.

statusSeq.description: The status counter after this change.

InstanceHealthState.description: Health of an instance as read now. Closed.

oneOf.description: Nothing is known, or the last observation is too old.
Everything works.
It works with problems.
It does not work.

InstanceLastFailure.description: How the last start, init, or run failed.

at.description: When it happened; null after a daemon restart.

code.description: The failure code, such as `process_exited` or `crash_loop`.

excerpt.description:
At most ten redacted lines from the end of the process output,
stderr first, each at most 256 characters.

exitCode.description: The exit code, if the process exited.

signal.description: The signal number, if a signal ended the process.

InstanceLifecycle.description:
The lifecycle of an instance (PRD section 19.1). Closed: `unknown` is a
real state and the set is fixed, so a new value is a protocol major.

oneOf.description: Created; the data folder is not initialized yet.
The data folder is being initialized.
Not running.
The process is starting.
The process runs.
The process is stopping.
Initialization, a start, or the process failed.
The process crashed and is being restarted.
The identity of the process is lost; it is never signalled.
Removed with its data kept.

InstanceLockState.description: Whether the instance lock is held, as a probe saw it. Open.

oneOf.description: Nobody holds the lock.
A process holds the lock.
A state this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

InstanceOwnership.description:
How an instance came to be managed here. Open. Not the registry column
`instances.ownership` (where the data came from: `created`, later
`restored` and `adopted`, spec 0005), and not the `Ownership` of an
environment in the domain (`Dedicated` or `Shared`): this says whether
a person runs the instance by hand or an environment owns it. `stacklyd`
sends `manual` until feature 44 adds environment membership.

oneOf.description: A person starts and stops it.
A value this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

InstancePage.description:
Reply of `instance.list`: ordered by name, then ID, without retained
instances.

next.description:
The cursor of the next page, to send back as `before`; null on the
last page. A page stops before its JSON passes
[`INSTANCE_PAGE_BYTES_MAX`].

adoptable.description:
Whether a daemon restart can adopt the process; null until
readiness succeeded once.

adopted.description: True for a process the daemon found running after its own restart.

InstanceReadiness.description: Readiness as read now (`effective` at the time of the snapshot).

detail.description: Redacted text with more about the reason.

reason.description:
A snake case code saying why, such as `probe_ok` or
`daemon_restarted`.

InstanceReadinessState.description: Readiness of an instance as read now. Closed.

oneOf.description: Nothing is known, or the last observation is too old.
The process runs but does not accept work yet.
The instance accepts work.

InstanceRemoved.description:
Content of `instance.removed`: the instance row was deleted. The event's
revision is the last revision plus one, and a client drops the instance
from its list. No daemon sends it before feature 20.

exhausted.description: True after the budget ran out.

nextAttemptAt.description: When the next respawn happens, while one waits.

InstanceStateChanged.description:
Content of `instance.state_changed`: the instance after a batch that
raised its revision (create, lifecycle, desired state, an `Auto` port).
The event's resource is the instance and its revision the instance's.
A retained instance is announced with lifecycle `retained`.

InstanceSummary.description:
One instance, as `instance.get`, `instance.list`, and
`instance.state_changed` show it.

blocker.description: Why the instance is blocked, if it is.

displayName.description: The name to show, if the person gave one.

id.description: The instance ID, a lowercase UUID.

initialized.description:
Whether the data folder was initialized (`data_initialized_at` is
set). Absent in older daemons, which means true; read it through
[`InstanceSummary::is_initialized`]. It is an `Option` so the Swift
type is optional too: typeshare reads only a plain
`#[serde(default)]` as optional, and this default is true.

lastFailure.description: The last failure, if there was one.

leftoverProcesses.description:
PIDs of group members left after the last stop; reported, never
signalled.

logsUnavailable.description: True when the output of the running process cannot be read.

ownership.description: Who runs the instance. Absent in older daemons; read as `manual`.

revision.description: The revision of the registry row.

runtimeId.description: The runtime the instance runs on.

runtimeVersion.description: The exact version of that runtime.

statusSeq.description:
Counts the changes of the status fields per instance and per daemon
run, from 1; it starts again from 1 after a daemon restart.

Limits.description: The limits a daemon enforces, as sent in `HandshakeAccepted`.

eventBufferLen.description: Events a subscriber may fall behind before an overflow gap.

maxFrameBytes.description: Largest control frame payload, in bytes.

maxInFlightRequests.description: Most requests in flight per connection.

maxLogBatchBytes.description: Largest log batch payload, in bytes.

ListProvidersReply.description:
Reply of `catalog.list_providers`: every entry in display order, in one
page.

items.description:
Provider and invalid entries first, planned entries last; then
category, display name, and ID.

ListSecretsReply.description: Reply of `secret.list`: the cached rows, ordered by reference.

NeedsSecretBlocker.description:
The content of the `needsSecret` blocker of an instance (spec 0011,
*Needs secret*): the instance DTO of feature 10 carries it in its
`blocker` slot as `{type: needsSecret, content: ...}`.

references.description: Every reference that cannot be read, ordered by reference text.

NeedsSecretItem.description: One reference a resource needs and cannot read.

generateAllowed.description: Whether a generated value would work for it.

NeedsSecretReason.description: Why a reference needs a value. Open.

oneOf.description: The store holds no value.
The keychain is locked.
The user or the access list refused the read.
The store call did not start in time.
The OS has no store.
A reason this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

OperationAccepted.description:
The reply, or the part of the reply, of every method that starts an
operation (spec 0007, *Idempotency*). The method's own reply may wrap
it.

operation.description: The operation, as created or as it stands now.

replayed.description:
True when the idempotency key named an operation an earlier request
started, so nothing new ran.

created.description: What it created or claimed, in order.

OperationFailureInfo.description: Why an operation failed; only in state `failed`.

error.description: The error that ended the operation, with `operationId` set.

reason.description:
The engine's reason code, such as `step_failed`, `interrupted`, or
`abandoned`.

retryable.description:
True when a new operation with a new idempotency key may succeed.
It differs from `error.retryable`, which is about sending the same
request again.

OperationKind.description:
What an operation does: the kind codes of spec 0004. Open: a newer
daemon may add kinds, which older clients read as `unrecognized`.

oneOf.description: Install a managed runtime.
Register a runtime in a folder the user owns.
Remove a runtime.
Create an instance.
Start an instance.
Stop an instance.
Restart an instance.
Reload an instance's configuration.
Rename an instance.
Remove an instance and keep its data.
Delete an instance and its data.
Move an instance to another runtime.
Move an instance to another provider revision.
Back up an instance.
Restore an instance.
Bring an environment up.
Take an environment down.
Update Stackly itself; its resource is the manager.
Migrate an instance's data to another line.

OperationPage.description: Reply of `operation.list`: newest first, by creation time then ID.

next.description:
The cursor of the next page, to send back as `before`; null on the
last page.

OperationProgress.description: How far an operation got. Closed.

oneOf.description: The work does not know how much is left.
The work counted what it did and what there is.

partial.description:
The items that did not all go to plan; a client shows the operation
as partial when this is not empty.

resources.description: The resources the operation created or changed.

OperationState.description:
The state of an operation (PRD section 18.2). Closed: a new state is a
new protocol major.

oneOf.description: Waiting to run, either new or resumed.
Running.
A cancel was asked for; the operation winds down.
Finished with success; final.
Finished with a failure; final.
Cancelled; final.
Stopped in a way it cannot recover from on its own; see `recovery`.

autoCompensatedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon undid on its own when it started.

interruptedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon found interrupted when it started.

maxQueued.description: The most operations that wait in the queue.

maxRunning.description: The most operations that run at once.

rejectedQueueFull.description:
Requests refused with `operation.queue_full` since the daemon
started.

resumedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon resumed on its own when it started.

OperationStepInfo.description:
One step of an operation's journal. The step's checkpoint is never
sent.

attempts.description: How many times the step started, at least 1.

errorCode.description: The catalog code of the step's failure; only in state `failed`.

finishedAt.description: When the step ended; null while it runs.

repeatable.description: Whether the engine may run the step again after an interruption.

reversible.description: Whether the engine can undo the step.

OperationSummary.description:
One operation as every client sees it, in replies and in both
operation events.

cancelRequestedAt.description: When a cancel was asked for.

failure.description: Why the operation failed; only in state `failed`.

id.description: The operation ID, a lowercase UUID v7.

pointOfNoReturnAt.description:
When the first step that cannot be undone started. From then on a
cancel no longer stops the work.

recovery.description: What needs the person's action; only in state `needs_recovery`.

resource.description:
The resource the operation works on; null for `update_manager`
before it names the manager.

result.description: What the operation produced, once it ended or was abandoned.

revision.description: The operation's revision; every committed change raises it.

stage.description: What the operation is doing now, such as `downloading`.

startedAt.description: When the operation first started running.

state.description: The state, one of the seven of PRD section 18.2.

waitingOn.description:
The operation this one waits for while queued: the oldest one that
holds or waits for one of its locks.

client.description: The kind of client that sent the request; null for the daemon.

origin.description: A request, or the daemon itself.

PartialItem.description: One item of a partial result, such as one leftover of an abandon.

code.description: A catalog code that explains the outcome, if any.

item.description: What the item is, such as a created item's reference.

resource.description: The resource the item belongs to, if any.

PartialOutcome.description: What happened to one item of a partial result. Open.

oneOf.description: Done, or cleaned up.
Failed, or cleaning it up failed.
Left alone on purpose, such as an item another operation owns.
Still there; the person decides what to do with it.
An outcome this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

PlatformCapabilityStatus.description: One platform capability (spec 0004) and its support.

reason.description: Why not, when it is not supported.

PlatformNoteDto.description: What the catalog says about one OS a provider has no artifact for.

ProtocolVersion.description:
Version of the IPC protocol a peer speaks.

`major` changes when the wire breaks, `minor` when it only gains optional
additions. Peers with the same major always talk, whatever their minors.

major.description: Bumped for every breaking change to the wire.

oneOf.description: Run more than one instance side by side.
Keep data across restarts.
Reload the configuration without a restart.
Expose metrics.
Serve TLS.
Back up while the instance is stopped.
Back up while the instance runs.
Back up as a logical dump.
A capability this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

ProviderCategory.description: The category of a provider. Open.

oneOf.description: A database server.
A message broker.
An analytics store.
A cache.
A proxy.
A test provider.
A category this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

ProviderDetail.description:
Reply of `catalog.get_provider`: one entry with its versions, its
artifacts, and what is wrong with it.

capabilities.description:
The eight capabilities in [`ProviderCapability::ALL`] order; empty
for planned and invalid entries.

issues.description: What failed validation; only for invalid entries.

manifestSha256.description:
The digest of the provider package, 64 lowercase hex characters;
null for planned and invalid entries.

note.description: The note of a planned entry.

platformNotes.description: What the catalog says about an OS without artifacts.

software.description:
The software the provider runs; null for planned and invalid
